problem: LLM-based universal navigation agents are jointly trained on fixed task sets and suffer catastrophic forgetting when new scenes or instruction styles (VLN/OLN/DUN) arrive sequentially. Existing LoRA and MoE-LoRA continual methods either ignore task-shared knowledge or assume a fixed number of experts.
motivation: Humans accumulate knowledge and reuse it to learn new skills, whereas retraining on all old data is costly. A lifelong navigation agent must therefore transfer shared knowledge, keep task-specific knowledge separated, and work without a task-id at test time.
key_idea: Decouple navigation knowledge into a shared LoRA subspace A and incrementally added per-task expert subspaces B (DE-LoRA), with knowledge inheritance, expert co-activation, orthogonality constraints, per-style chain-of-thought, and task-aware retrieval of experts at test time.
insight: Ablations show every component contributes: removing NSCoT drops SR from 67.3 to 51.1 with forgetting rising from 4.3 to 27.3, and removing ECAS drops SR to 58.1. The retrieval ablation shows instruction-only matching collapses (SR 35.0), observation-only is close (65.1), and mixed matching is best (67.3), so expert selection quality matters most in task-id-agnostic inference. Notably, the strongest baselines (O-LoRA and SD-LoRA) already reach 58-59 SR only when paired with the authors' TAKA, so much of the gain over naive MoE-LoRA comes from task-aware retrieval.
method: DE-LoRA: one shared low-rank matrix A across all tasks plus a growing set of expert B matrices; the output adds the top-K activated B·A·x terms (K=2, r=16), and a new B is added per task.
Knowledge Inheritance Strategy (KIS): initialize the new expert B_t from PCA of earlier experts with the same instruction style, using the mean plus the average of the top-r principal directions.
Experts Co-Activation Strategy (ECAS): during training, the trainable B_t is co-activated with K-1 frozen related experts in the forward pass, so previous knowledge is reused.
Shared Smoothing Consolidation (SSC) loss: a Fisher-weighted (EWC-style) penalty on changes to shared A, with the Fisher matrix updated by EMA (ω=0.9, λ=0.1).
Expert Subspace Orthogonality Constraint (ESOC): penalize the trace inner product between L2-normalized B_t and all previous B_i so experts stay decoupled.
Navigation-Specific CoT (NSCoT): separate chain-of-thought reasoning templates for VLN (progress tracking), OLN (infer the target object), and DUN (parse the dialogue for intent).

Task-Aware Knowledge Aggregation (TAKA): store CLIP scene and instruction embeddings per task; at test time, mask tasks by instruction similarity > μ=0.5, rank by observation similarity, and activate the top-K experts without a task-id.

setting.training_data: Self-built LENL benchmark on Matterport3D: 15 sequential tasks (one scene each, VLN/OLN/DUN styles, ~228-1848 train instructions per task), with 3 held-out unseen-scene tasks; the NaviLLM pretrained model is the starting point
setting.observation: egocentric RGB panoramic views encoded by CLIP ViT (CLS features)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints generated as LLM action tokens (NaviLLM style)
setting.privileged: none (the task-id is used only during training; the stored retrieval embeddings of training tasks are used at test time)

numbers.method: Uni-Walker (S1-S15 plus unseen S16-S18, avg. over 18 tasks)
numbers.extra: Lifelong sequential training, task-id agnostic testing; avg over 18 tasks including 3 unseen-scene tasks
numbers.evidence: Table 1/SR & SR-F, appendix Tables SPL/OSR: Avg. 66, 61, 81; forgetting 5, 7, 5

numbers.extra: Unseen scenes, no training on them
numbers.evidence: Table Results (SR%) for Generalization: Avg 62.0 (S16 74, S17 61, S18 51)

numbers_note: The benchmark is the authors' own LENL benchmark, not a standard one; all numbers are averages over its tasks. Average rows in Table 1 are integer-rounded; the ablation tables give one-decimal values on the 15 continual tasks.
results: On the LENL benchmark Uni-Walker achieves avg SR 66 / SPL 61 / OSR 81 with forgetting of only 5 / 7 / 5, beating the strongest baseline SD-LoRA+TAKA (SR 59, SPL 38, OSR 79; forgetting 16 / 42 / 7). On unseen scenes it gets 62.0 SR vs 57.0 for SD-LoRA+TAKA, and it also outperforms NaviLLM, ScaleVLN and SAME (avg SR 50, 53 and 55).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulated Matterport3D discrete environments with a self-built benchmark of 18 tasks, with no real-robot test.

Storage and retrieval grow linearly with the number of tasks (one expert plus Fisher matrix per task, and stored CLIP embeddings), and inference relies on similarity matching that may fail for very similar tasks.
Strong baselines (O-LoRA, SD-LoRA) are augmented with the authors' own TAKA, and the benchmark is small, so gains may partly reflect the benchmark design.
